sources.entry: Tusk - Unofficial, third-party, community driven Evernote app with a handful of useful features.

summary.one_liner: Tusk is an unofficial, open source, community-driven desktop client for Evernote with themes, keyboard shortcuts, and note export features.
summary.what_it_does: Tusk is a third-party Evernote desktop app built for Linux, macOS, and other platforms, distributed via GitHub Releases, Snapcraft, and Homebrew Cask. It offers Black, Dark, and Sepia themes, plus Focus, Compact, and Auto-Night display modes. Users can customize local and global keyboard shortcuts (70+ local shortcuts listed), stored in ~/.tusk.json. Notes can be exported as PDF, HTML, or Markdown, and the app supports drag-and-drop file attachment, note navigation by keyboard, zoom scaling, and Yinxiang login. The README also describes a development setup using npm or yarn.
use_cases: Use Evernote notes on Linux desktop
Export Evernote notes to PDF, HTML, or Markdown
Access Evernote from a dark or sepia-themed interface
Quickly capture notes from anywhere with global shortcuts
how_to_run: Download the installer for your system from the GitHub Releases page
macOS: brew cask install tusk (may not be the latest version)
Development: git clone your fork, then cd tusk
Install dependencies: npm install or yarn install
Run in dev mode: npm start or yarn start
notable: Unofficial, community-driven Evernote client that Evernote lists as an alternative for Linux
Local and global customizable keyboard shortcuts via ~/.tusk.json
Export notes as PDF, HTML, or Markdown
Black, Dark, Sepia themes with Focus, Compact, and Auto-Night modes
caveats: Unofficial and not affiliated with Evernote
Homebrew Cask version may lag behind the latest release; Snapcraft is officially maintained
Global shortcuts must be enabled manually via the File menu
